subject: Hosting intake — security & egress acceptance
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medicorp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting intake — technical details & egress requirements

Hi Connor + team,

Thanks again for the quick sync today. Per our notes, I wanted to capture the immediate technical asks from our infra/security teams so you can route to the right owners: 

- Egress IPs: We need a static set of outbound IPs for allowlisting third-party healthcare APIs (HHS endpoints). Preferably a /29 — see attached egres-ip-list.csv as a starting point.
- VPC connectivity: We will peer via a dedicated VPC peering connection (no transit gateway) and expect BGP-style route advertisements on our side.
- KMS / encryption: Keys are managed by our KMS (AWS KMS). We will require Redwood to support customer-managed keys for data-at-rest and key rotation notifications.
- Audit logs: SOC2 team requires 90 days of write-once audit logs for inference requests and admin operations.
- Data residency: All inference traffic must remain in us-east-1; control plane can be in another region but metadata and logs must be stored in region.

Attachments: MediCorp_VPC_Diagram.pdf, egress-ip-list.csv

Next steps: can you confirm who owns the egress/static IP allocation on Redwood's side, and whether your runtime supports BYOK/KMS integration for Private deployments?

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Infrastructure — MediCorp Health
ops@medicorp.com

---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medicorp.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting intake — technical details & egress requirements

Sanjay, thanks — noted. Quick answers up front and a suggestion for next steps: 

- Static egress: For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) we can present a customer-dedicated NAT egress pool. We can reserve a /29 for you — I will confirm allocation window with ProdInfra.
- VPC connectivity: We support direct VPC peering and route exchange. Our networking team prefers IP prefixes pushed from your side; we'll provide the peer ASN and preferred CIDR(s).
- KMS / BYOK: Yes — we support customer-managed keys using AWS KMS and HSM-backed integration for on-prem packages. We will need a key ARN and a cross-account IAM role for encrypt/decrypt operations.
- Audit logs: We can stream inference request logs to an S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock for 90-day WORM retention. Will include an example retention configuration.
- Residency: We can pin the inference runtime to us-east-1 workers and provision regional data stores per the onboarding plan.

Proposed next step: technical deep dive with our networking + security SMEs. Can we set a 60-minute call tomorrow to walk the diagram and confirm BGP/peering details and the egress IP allocation timeline?

Connor O'Brien
Technical Account Manager — Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132

---

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medicorp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@medicorp.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting intake — technical details & egress requirements

Connor — that works. Adding Elena (network lead) to the thread. We can do 60 minutes tomorrow 10:00–11:00 PT. Key clarifications from our side before the call: 

- We will provide a primary ASN and the peering CIDR. Do you support a single-point-of-failure-free design (two peers across different AZs)?
- On KMS: our compliance team would prefer an envelope encryption flow where Redwood never receives the plaintext key. Is that supported?
- Logs: we need proof-of-concept of the S3 Object Lock configuration and a sample policy.

Also attaching a redacted list of third-party endpoints that must be allowlisted. Please confirm if Redwood can take responsibility for maintaining the egress list on its NAT pool when we provide updates (anticipated quarterly).

Best,
Sanjay

Attachments: egres-ip-list.csv (updated)

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medicorp.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hosting intake — technical details & egress requirements

Hi Sanjay / Elena — thanks for the detail. Following up from our internal SME sync: 

- Dual-peer design: yes, we can configure redundant NAT peers across two AZs. We will expose a primary and secondary egress IP set; failover is handled by our gateway layer. We'll document RTO for failover in the runbook.
- Envelope encryption: supported. We use a sealed-envelope approach where your KMS signs an encryption key and we never persist the plaintext root key. We'll include the exact flow in the security annex.
- S3 Object Lock POC: attaching a sample lifecycle/policy snippet and a short runbook excerpt that demonstrates the WORM retention configuration.
- Egress list ops: Redwood can own the egress NAT pool and apply allowlist changes on a quarterly cadence or ad-hoc with a 48-hour SLA if changes are critical. We'll include an authorization matrix for who can request urgent updates.

Action items (owners):
- Ben Carter to confirm /29 allocation timeline with ProdInfra (owner: Ben) — ETA 48 hours.
- Connor to schedule technical deep dive and send calendar invite (owner: Connor) — DONE.
- Kimberly to draft security annex and sample KMS flow for SOC2 review (owner: Kimberly) — ETA 3 business days.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleSharedDrive (designs and POC snippets)

Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
